canonical.title: The validation & schema layer for React forms in 2026: Zod 4, Valibot, ArkType — and why Standard Schema changed the question

siblings.title: The React form-library landscape in 2026: RHF still wins, TanStack Form is the real challenger, Formik is a zombie
siblings.summary: React Hook Form (v7.81.0, 58M weekly downloads, v8 in beta) remains the default; TanStack Form 1.33.2 is the credible challenger with a framework-agnostic core and better path types but self-admitted verbosity; Conform owns progressive-enhancement forms; Formik is a zombie and React Final Form is in maintenance limbo.

siblings.title: React's native form primitives in 2026: what they replace, and what they don't
siblings.summary: React's form primitives froze at 19.0 and are a submission layer, not a form layer — they own pending/error/optimistic state across the network boundary, and own nothing about the fields.

siblings.title: The hard parts of React forms in 2026: arrays, conditionals, wizards, and the render budget
siblings.summary: Where the three mainstream React form libraries actually break on field arrays, conditional fields, dependent async validation, wizards, and 100+ field forms — with the API-level specifics that decide it.

siblings.title: Wiring form engines into React UI kits in 2026
siblings.summary: The UI kits stopped picking a form engine for you: shadcn's Field, Base UI's Field and React Aria are all engine-agnostic layout/a11y primitives, and the real cost is the per-component Controller/field.state bridge you still hand-write.

siblings.title: Testing React forms in 2026: which tier catches what
siblings.summary: The 2026 form-testing stack is Vitest + schema unit tests + jsdom component tests, with Browser Mode as the real middle tier and Playwright reserved for the three or four flows that actually touch the network.

siblings.title: Uploads, autosave and unsaved-changes guards in React forms (2026)
siblings.summary: Bytes bypass your form: the browser presigns and uploads direct-to-storage while the form only carries a key — and progress still means XHR, not fetch.

sources.title: Standard Schema
sources.claim: Standard Schema is a family of TypeScript specs (StandardSchemaV1) authored by the Zod, Valibot and ArkType maintainers to let tools accept any compliant schema without adapters.

sources.title: standard-schema/spec — README
sources.claim: The StandardSchemaV1 Issue interface carries only `message` and `path` — no error code, no params — so a consumer of Standard Schema cannot re-translate errors itself; v1.1 adds StandardTypedV1 and StandardJSONSchemaV1.

sources.title: npm — @standard-schema/spec
sources.claim: @standard-schema/spec reached 1.0.0 on 2025-01-27 and 1.1.0 on 2025-12-15; it is the version in use in July 2026.

sources.title: Zod 4 — release notes
sources.claim: Zod 4 is 14.71x faster at string parsing, 7.43x at arrays, 6.5x at objects vs Zod 3; core bundle drops from 12.47kb to 5.36kb; tsc instantiation blowups on .extend()/.omit() chains drop from ~4000ms to ~400ms.

sources.title: Zod — error customization
sources.claim: Zod 4 unifies error customisation behind a single `error` param with precedence schema-level > per-parse > global (z.config) > locale, and ships 40+ locales in zod/locales.

sources.title: Zod — API reference
sources.claim: z.coerce.* schemas have an input type of `unknown` by default; z.stringbool() parses "true"/"1"/"yes".

sources.title: Zod Mini
sources.claim: Zod Mini is a tree-shakable, functional variant: 2.12kb vs 5.91kb for a simple schema, at the cost of a more verbose .check()-based API.

sources.title: Valibot — comparison guide
sources.claim: For a login-form schema Valibot bundles to 1.37 kB vs Zod's 17.7 kB (esbuild) and Zod Mini's 6.88 kB; Valibot's runtime speed is 'midfield'.

sources.title: Valibot — pipelines
sources.claim: Valibot composes validation and transformation with v.pipe(), which must start with a schema; transformation actions change both value and type.

sources.title: Valibot — internationalization
sources.claim: Valibot ships @valibot/i18n as modular submodules plus setGlobalMessage/setSchemaMessage/setSpecificMessage with specific > schema > global precedence.

sources.title: ArkType — integrations
sources.claim: ArkType co-authored Standard Schema and integrates with react-hook-form, tRPC 11+, Hono, oRPC and drizzle-arktype.

sources.title: ArkType — expressions
sources.claim: ArkType handles string-to-typed-data with morphs: type("string.numeric.parse"), .pipe(), and filter (pre-morph) vs narrow (post-morph).

sources.title: ArkType — configuration
sources.claim: ArkType customises errors via arktype/config and .configure() per type (shallow only); it has no locales package and its docs call i18n 'still a topic we're working on'.

sources.title: @hookform/resolvers
sources.claim: @hookform/resolvers v5 ships a generic standardSchemaResolver alongside 20 library-specific resolvers; ArkType's dedicated resolver is firstError-only and Joi cannot infer values at all.

sources.title: TanStack Form — validation guide
sources.claim: TanStack Form accepts any Standard Schema library natively with no adapter, but its validators do not hand back transformed values.

sources.title: next-safe-action — Standard Schema
sources.claim: next-safe-action validates Server Actions against any Standard Schema v1 library with no adapter, calling schema['~standard'].validate(input) directly.

sources.title: Next.js — forms guide
sources.claim: Next.js 16's official forms guide still hard-codes Zod for Server Action validation — and the sample still uses the removed Zod v3 `invalid_type_error` option.

sources.title: Conform — parseWithZod
sources.claim: Conform's parseWithZod strips empty values and coerces FormData strings to the schema's types by introspecting the schema.

sources.title: Valibot vs Zod 2026: I half-migrated and stopped
sources.claim: A practitioner migrating two forms to Valibot saved ~18 KB gzipped and ~140 ms LCP, but kept Zod server-side because drizzle-valibot lagged drizzle-zod.

sources.title: pkgpulse — Zod v4 vs ArkType vs TypeBox vs Valibot (2026)
sources.claim: 5-field object validation ~8M ops/s ArkType, ~4M Valibot, ~2M Zod v4, ~300K Zod v3; ArkType ~20 KB gzipped and its compile time can become the bottleneck on very large schemas.

sources.title: Yup
sources.claim: Yup 1.7 is Standard Schema compatible, so it plugs into any Standard-Schema-consuming form library.

sources.title: Joi — API reference
sources.claim: Joi 18 implements the Standard Schema `~standard` property including the JSON Schema converter, and depends on @standard-schema/spec ^1.1.0.

sources.title: ArkType
sources.claim: ArkType markets itself as 'TypeScript's 1:1 validator, optimized from editor to runtime' and claims ~20x faster runtime validation than Zod.

sources.title: npm — zod
sources.claim: Zod's latest release is 4.4.3 (July 2026); npm reports ~224M weekly downloads — more than react itself (~153M/week).

sources.title: npm — valibot
sources.claim: Valibot's latest release is 1.4.2 (July 2026), ~14.3M weekly npm downloads.

sources.title: npm — arktype
sources.claim: ArkType's latest release is 2.2.3 (July 2026), ~1.2M weekly npm downloads.

sources.title: npm — yup
sources.claim: Yup's latest release is 1.7.1 (July 2026), ~10.1M weekly npm downloads.

sources.title: npm — joi
sources.claim: Joi's latest release is 18.2.3 (July 2026), ~17.8M weekly npm downloads, and it now depends on @standard-schema/spec.

sources.title: Valibot — toNumber
sources.claim: Valibot ships first-class coercion actions such as toNumber() and toDate() for use inside v.pipe().

sources.title: Conform
sources.claim: Conform is a FormData-first, progressively-enhanced form library for Remix/Next.js that runs one schema on both client and server.

sources.title: next-safe-action
sources.claim: next-safe-action is the dominant typed Server-Action wrapper and is Standard-Schema-native.

sources.title: npm — @hookform/resolvers
sources.claim: @hookform/resolvers v5.4.0 (May 2026) is the current release and infers input and output types from the underlying schema.

sources.title: Zod — error formatting
sources.claim: Zod 4 replaces ZodError.flatten()/.format() with the top-level z.flattenError() and z.treeifyError().
